current.text: Washington added Anthony Davis, Trae Young and AJ Dybantsa. All three missed last season.
Trae Young re-signed with Washington. The speaker sees the deal as a possible overpay.
Projected starters are Trae Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa, Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr.
The fifth starter spot is not settled. Kyshawn George holds it on the depth chart, but many wings compete for it.
Anthony Davis plays center on offense. Alex Sarr moves to power forward, plays further from the basket and switches on the perimeter.
Trae Young and Anthony Davis will take most of the usage. Little is left for AJ Dybantsa and the young players.
Alex Sarr loses usage to Davis, Young and Dybantsa. Davis also takes rebound and block chances from him.
Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr limit Bilal Coulibaly's minutes and rim contests.
Deandre Ayton comes off the bench as the backup center.
The roster is deep and flexible, with many long wings and a crowded group of guards. Expect a 10 or 11 man rotation, with 12 or 13 players who could justify minutes.
The rebuild is over. The team is trying to win and will push for the play-in.
Late-season resting and minutes cuts of past years should not return this season.
Ben predicts around 40 wins, near .500 and in the play-in mix. The market win total of 35.5 is lower than that.
Health is a key factor for the team, and Anthony Davis's health is the main question.
The speaker is about 80% sure the Wizards keep Anthony Davis and try to make the playoffs, but a trade cannot be ruled out.
If Anthony Davis is traded, Alex Sarr starts at center.
Defense is the main question after the team was the worst in the league last year. Steve Clifford joined the coaching staff to help.
Head coach Brian Keefe is under the most pressure to win games this season.
The team chases the play-in and has only one back-to-back in the fantasy playoff weeks, so rest risk for its stars in weeks 19 to 21 looks low.

tags.name: win-now team
tags.detail: Rebuild over, pushing for the play-in. Late-season rest and minutes cuts are not expected.
tags.new_meaning: The team is trying to win games this season, so late-season tanking and resting of healthy players are unlikely.

tags.name: deep rotation
tags.detail: 10 or 11 man rotation expected, with 12 or 13 players who could justify minutes. Crowded at wing and guard.
tags.new_meaning: The team is expected to play 10 or more players, so minutes are spread thin beyond the top options.

tags.name: concentrated usage
tags.detail: Trae Young and Anthony Davis take most of the usage. Little is left for Dybantsa, Sarr and the young players.
tags.new_meaning: A few stars take most of the team's shots and touches, which caps the usage of the other players.

note: Washington is trying to win now, so Trae Young and Anthony Davis get most of the usage and late-season rest risk is low. Alex Sarr, AJ Dybantsa and the young wings lose usage, and Sarr also loses rebounds and blocks while he plays power forward next to Davis. Early on, watch Davis's health and any trade talk, since Sarr starts at center if Davis leaves, and watch who wins the fifth starter spot among the wings.
